A.subject: Physics
A.text: Consider the efficiency of carnot's engine is given by η = (αβ/sin θ) log e (βx/kT), where a and β are constants. If T is temperature, k is Boltzmann constant, θ is angular displacement and x has the dimensions of length. Then, choose the incorrect option
options: Dimensions of β is same as that of force.
Dimensions of α^(-1) x is same as that of energy.
Dimensions of η^(-1) sin θ is same as that of αβ.
Dimensions of α is same as that of β.
A.sol_text:
(1) [β] = [kT/x] = [E/x] = [MLT^(-2)] = [F] ✓
(2) [α,β] = [M^a L^b T^d]
[α]^(-1) = [β] = [kT/x]
so [α]^(-1)[x] = [kT] = [ML^2T^(-2)] = energy ✓
(3) η sin θ = αβ
so [η sin θ] = [αβ]
[η] = [M^a L^b T^d] it is dimensionless quantity ✓
(4) [α] ≠ [β]

A.subject: Physics
A.text: At time t = 0 a particle starts travelling from a height 72 cm in a plane keeping z coordinate constant. At any instant of time its position along the x and y directions are defined at 3t and 5t^3 respectively. At t = 1 s acceleration of the particle will be

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A pressure-pump has a horizontal tube of cross sectional area 10 cm² for the outflow of water at a speed of 20 m/s. The force exerted on the vertical wall just in front of the tube which stops water horizontally flowing out of the tube, is [given: density of water = 1000 kg/m³]

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A uniform metal chain of mass m and length 'L' passes over a massless and frictionless pulley. It is released from rest with a part of its length 'ℓ' is hanging on one side and rest of its length 'L - ℓ' is hanging on the other side of the pulley. At a certain point of time, when ℓ = L/x, the acceleration of the chain is g/2. The value of x is ______.
A.sol_text: For a chain over a pulley with lengths ℓ and (L - ℓ) on each side, using the analogy with two masses: m₁ = (m/L)ℓ and m₂ = (m/L)(L - ℓ). The acceleration is a = (m₂ - m₁)/(m₁ + m₂) × g = ((L - ℓ) - ℓ)/L × g = (L - 2ℓ)/L × g. Given a = g/2 and ℓ = L/x: g/2 = (L - 2(L/x))/L × g. Simplifying: 1/2 = (L - 2L/x)/L = 1 - 2/x. Therefore: 2/x = 1/2, which gives x = 4.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A bullet of mass 200 g having initial kinetic energy 90 J is shot inside a long swimming pool as shown in the figure. If its kinetic energy reduces to 40 J within 1 s, the minimum length of the pool, the bullet has to travel so that it completely comes to rest is
A.sol_text: Given: m = 200 g = 0.2 kg, initial KE = 90 J, KE after 1 s = 40 J. From (1/2)mv^2 = 90, we get v = 30 m/s. From (1/2)mv^2 = 40, we get v = 20 m/s. Deceleration a = (20 - 30)/1 = -10 m/s^2. Using v^2 = u^2 + 2as with final velocity = 0: 0 = 30^2 + 2(-10)s, so s = 900/20 = 45 m.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Assume there are two identical simple pendulum clocks. Clock - 1 is placed on the earth and Clock - 2 is placed on a space station located at a height h above the earth surface. Clock - 1 and Clock - 2 operate at time periods 4 s and 6 s respectively. Then the value of h is- (consider radius of earth RE = 6400 km and g on earth 10 m/s²)
A.sol_text: T ∝ sqrt(l/g). For identical pendulums: T1/T2 = sqrt(g2/g1) = R/(R+h). Given T1 = 4 s and T2 = 6 s. So 4/6 = R/(R+h). Solving: (R+h)/R = 6/4 = 3/2. Therefore R+h = 1.5R, which gives h = 0.5R = 0.5 × 6400 = 3200 km.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Consider a cylindrical tank of radius 1 m is filled with water. The top surface of water is at 15 m from the bottom of the cylinder. There is a hole on the wall of cylinder at a height of 5 m from the bottom. A force of 5 × 10^5 N is applied on the top surface of water using a piston. The speed of outflow from the hole will be: (given atmosphere pressure P_A = 1.01 × 10^5 Pa, density of water ρ_w = 1000 kg/m^3 and gravitational acceleration g = 10 m/s^2)
A.sol_text: By Bernoulli's theorem, apply between top surface and hole: (5×10^5)/(π(1)^2) + ρg(10) = 1.01×10^5 + (1/2)ρ(v)^2. Solving: v^2 = 200 + 10^6/(1000π) - 202. Therefore v ≈ 17.8 m/s

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A vessel contains 14 g of nitrogen gas at a temperature of 27°C. The amount of heat to be transferred to the gas to double the r.m.s speed of its molecules will be; Take R = 8.32 J mol^(-1) K^(-1).
A.sol_text: n = 0.5 mol, T = 300 K. For v_rms to be doubled: T' = 4 × 300 = 1200 K. ΔT = 900 K. Heat transferred = n × C_v × ΔT = (0.5) × (5/2) × (8.32) × (900) = 9360 J

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A slab of dielectric constant K has the same cross-sectional area as the plates of a parallel plate capacitor and thickness (3/4)d, where d is the separation of the plates. The capacitance of the capacitor when the slab is inserted between the plates will be: (Given C0 = capacitance of capacitor with air as medium between plates.)
A.sol_text: C0 = (ε0*A)/d. When dielectric slab of thickness (3/4)d is inserted, the effective separation becomes: d - (3/4)d + (3/4)d/K = (1/4)d + (3/4)d/K = (d/4)(1 + 3/K) = d(K+3)/(4K). Therefore C = (ε0*A)/[d(K+3)/(4K)] = (4ε0*A*K)/(d(K+3)) = (4K*C0)/(3+K)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A uniform electric field E = (8m/e) V/m is created between two parallel plates of length 1 m as shown in figure, (where m = mass of electron and e = charge of electron). An electron enters the field symmetrically between the plates with a speed of 2 m/s. The angle of deviation (θ) of the path of the electron as it comes out of the field will be
A.sol_text: Given: E = (8m/e) V/m, length l = 1 m, initial speed v_x = 2 m/s, acceleration a_y = -8 m/s^2. Time in field: t = l/v_x = 1/2 s. Final vertical velocity: v_y = a_y × t = -8 × (1/2) = -4 m/s. Angle of deviation: tan(θ) = |v_y|/v_x = 4/2 = 2. Therefore θ = tan^(-1)(2).

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: A uniform wire of resistance 80 Ω is cut into four equal parts. These parts are now connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance of the combination will be 5 Ω. Statement II: Two resistances 2R and 3R are connected in parallel in an electric circuit. The value of thermal energy developed in 3R and 2R will be in the ratio 3:2. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the option given below.
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
A.sol_text: Statement I: Each part has resistance = 80/4 = 20 Ω. When 4 equal resistances of 20 Ω are connected in parallel: R_eff = 20/4 = 5 Ω. Statement I is CORRECT. Statement II: For parallel connection, voltage across both is same. Thermal energy H = (AV)^2/R. Ratio = H_3R/H_2R = (AV)^2/3R divided by (AV)^2/2R = 2/3, which is NOT 3:2. Statement II is INCORRECT.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A triangular shaped wire carrying 10 A current is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T, as shown in figure. The magnetic force on segment CD is (Given BC = BD = 5 cm).
A.sol_text: F = i l × B = i(Bsin60°) = 10 × (5/100) × 0.5 × sqrt(3)/2 = 10 × 0.05 × 0.5 × 0.866 = 0.2165 N ≈ 0.216 N. The force on segment CD is calculated using the magnetic force formula where the effective length is CD and the angle between CD and magnetic field is 60°.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The magnetic field at the center of current carrying circular loop is B1. The magnetic field at a distance of sqrt(3) times radius of the given circular loop from the center on its axis is B2. The value of B1/B2 will be

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A transformer operating at primary voltage 8 kV and secondary voltage 160 V serves a load of 80 kW. Assuming the transformer to be ideal with purely resistive load and working on unity power factor, the loads in the primary and secondary circuit would be
A.sol_text: For ideal transformer with power P = 80 kW: Primary current i1 = P/V1 = (80×1000)/8000 = 10 A. Secondary current i2 = P/V2 = (80×1000)/160 = 500 A. Primary resistance R1 = V1/i1 = 8000/10 = 800 Ω. Secondary resistance R2 = V2/i2 = 160/500 = 0.32 Ω.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Sun light falls normally on a surface of area 36 cm^2 and exerts an average force of 7.2 × 10^-9 N within a time period of 20 minutes. Considering a case of complete absorption, the energy flux of incident light is
A.sol_text: Using Pressure = (1/c) and F/A = (1/c), we get I = (F × c)/(A) = (7.2 × 10^-9 × 3 × 10^8)/(36 × 10^-4) = (2160 × 10^-1)/(36 × 10^-4) = 60000 × 10^-4 = 0.6 W/cm^2 = 0.06 W/cm^2 (converting to proper units). The energy flux (intensity) I = 0.06 W/cm^2

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The power of a lens (biconvex) is 1.25 m^(-1) in particular medium. Refractive index of the lens is 1.5 and radii of curvature are 20 cm and 40 cm respectively. The refractive index of surrounding medium is?
A.sol_text: Using lens maker formula: 1/f = (μ₂/μ₁ - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂). Given: Power = 1.25 m^(-1), so f = 1/1.25 = 0.8 m = 80 cm. Refractive index of lens μ₂ = 1.5, R₁ = 20 cm, R₂ = -40 cm. Substituting: 1.25/100 = (1.5/μ₁ - 1)(1/20 + 1/40) = (1.5/μ₁ - 1)(3/40). Therefore: 1/80 = (1.5/μ₁ - 1) × (3/40). Solving: 1.5/μ₁ - 1 = 1/6, so 1.5/μ₁ = 7/6, giving μ₁ = 9/7.

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
A.text: Two streams of photons, possessing energies equal to five and ten times the work function of metal are incident on the metal surface successively. The ratio of maximum velocities of the photoelectron emitted, in the two cases respectively, will be
A.sol_text: Using photoelectric effect equation: (1/2)mv^2 = E_photon - phi, where E is photon energy and phi is work function. For case 1: (1/2)mv1^2 = 5*phi - phi = 4*phi. For case 2: (1/2)mv2^2 = 10*phi - phi = 9*phi. Therefore v1^2/v2^2 = 4/9, which gives v1/v2 = 2/3.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A radioactive sample decays 7/8 times its original quantity in 15 minutes. The half life of the sample is
A.sol_text: Using radioactive decay formula: N = N0 / 2^(t/T_1/2). Given that N = N0/8 when t = 15 min. Therefore: N0/8 = N0 / 2^(15/T_1/2). This gives 2^(15/T_1/2) = 8 = 2^3. So 15/T_1/2 = 3, which means T_1/2 = 15/3 = 5 minutes.

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
A.text: An n.p.n. transistor with current gain beta = 100 in common emitter configuration is shown in figure. The output voltage of the amplifier will be
A.sol_text: For a common emitter amplifier, the voltage gain is given by: V_o/V_i = beta × (R_C/R_B). Given: beta = 100, R_C = 10 kΩ, R_B = 1 kΩ, V_i = 1 mV = 1 × 10^(-3) V. Therefore: V_o = 100 × (10/1) × 10^(-3) = 100 × 10 × 10^(-3) = 1000 × 10^(-3) = 1.0 V

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A FM broad cast transmitter, using modulating signal of frequency 20 kHz has a deviation ratio of 10. The Bandwidth required for transmission is
A.sol_text: For FM, Bandwidth B = 2(Δf + fm) where Δf is frequency deviation and fm is modulating frequency. Given: fm = 20 kHz, Δf/fm = 10 (deviation ratio). Therefore Δf = fm × 10 = 20 × 10 = 200 kHz. BW = 2(200 + 20) = 2(220) = 440 kHz

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of 19.6 m/s from the top of a tower. The ball strikes the ground after 6 s. The height from the ground up to which the ball can rise will be (k/5) m. The value of k is (use g = 9.8 m/s^2)
B.sol_text: Given: v = 19.6 m/s, t = 6s, g = 9.8 m/s^2. Time taken in upward motion above tower = 2s. Time taken from topmost point to ground = 4s. Using sqrt(2h/g) = 4, we get 2h/g = 16. Therefore h = 16 × 9.8 / 2 = 8 × 9.8. Since height = (k/5) m, we have k/5 = 8 × 9.8, so k = 8 × 9.8 × 5 = 392.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
B.text: The distance of centre of mass from end A of a one dimensional rod (AB) having mass density ρ = ρ0(1 - x^2/L^2) kg/m and length L (in meter) is 3L/α m. The value of α is ______. (where x is the distance from end A)
B.sol_text: Using center of mass formula: x_cm = ∫[A·ρ0(1 - x^2/L^2)·x dx from 0 to L] / ∫[A·ρ0(1 - x^2/L^2) dx from 0 to L]. Numerator: ∫(x - x^3/L^2)dx from 0 to L = L^2/2 - L^2/4 = L^2/4. Denominator: ∫(1 - x^2/L^2)dx from 0 to L = L - L/3 = 2L/3. Therefore x_cm = (L^2/4)/(2L/3) = (L^2/4)·(3/2L) = 3L/8. Comparing with 3L/α gives α = 8.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A string of area of cross-section 4 mm^2 and length 0.5 m is connected with a rigid body of mass 2 kg. The body is rotated in a vertical circular path of radius 0.5 m. The body acquires a speed of 5 m/s at the bottom of the circular path. Strain produced in the string when the body is at the bottom of the circle is ___ × 10^(-5). (use young's modulus 10^11 N/m^2 and g = 10 m/s^2)
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: At a certain temperature, the degrees of freedom per molecule for gas is 8. The gas performs 150 J of work when it expands under constant pressure. The amount of heat absorbed by the gas will be _______ J.
B.sol_text: Given: f = 8 (degrees of freedom), W = P dV = 150 J. For constant pressure process, Q = W + ΔU = P dV + (f/2) P dV = P dV(1 + f/2) = 150(1 + 8/2) = 150 × 5 = 750 J
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: The potential energy of a particle of mass 4 kg in motion along the x-axis is given by U = 4(1 - cos 4x) J. The time period of the particle for small oscillation (sin θ - θ) is (π/K) s. The value of K is _______.
B.sol_text: Given U = 4(1 - cos 4x). Force F = -dU/dx = -(4)(4 sin 4x) = -16 sin 4x. For small x, sin 4x ≈ 4x, so F = -16(4x) = -64x = -kx. Comparing with Hooke's law, k = 64. Time period T = 2π√(m/k) = 2π√(4/64) = 2π√(1/16) = 2π(1/4) = π/2. Given T = π/K, so π/2 = π/K, therefore K = 2.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: Zero orbital overlap is an out of phase overlap. Reason R: It results due to different orientation/direction of approach of orbitals. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
A.sol_text: Zero overlapping is a condition where there is no overlapping between two orbitals. The first condition is that the two orbitals should not be symmetrical and the second condition is that both orbitals should be in different planes. This occurs when the orbitals approach each other from different orientations/directions, resulting in out of phase overlap. Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
A.text: The correct decreasing order for metallic character is
A.sol_text: Metallic character increases from top to bottom in a group and decreases from left to right in a period. Na is from group 1 (more metallic), Mg from group 2 (less metallic than Na), Be comes above Mg hence less metallic than Mg, Si is more metallic than P. Order: Na > Mg > Be > Si > P

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
A.text: Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: The reduction of a metal oxide is easier if the metal formed is in liquid state than solid state. Reason R: The value of ΔG° becomes more on negative side as entropy is higher in liquid state than solid state. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
A.sol_text: Reduction of a metal oxide is easier when the metal is formed in liquid state because the entropy is higher in liquid state than solid state. Higher entropy makes ΔG° more negative (ΔG° = ΔH° - TΔS°), making the reduction process more thermodynamically favorable. Both assertion and reason are correct, and reason R correctly explains assertion A.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The products obtained during treatment of hard water using Clark's method are:
A.sol_text: Clark's method involves adding Ca(OH)2 to hard water containing Mg(HCO3)2 and Ca(HCO3)2. The reaction is: Mg(HCO3)2 + 2Ca(OH)2 → 2CaCO3↓ + Mg(OH)2↓ + 2H2O. This produces a precipitate of CaCO3 and Mg(OH)2, which can be filtered out to soften the water.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Statement-I: An alloy of lithium and magnesium is used to make aircraft plates. Statement-II: The magnesium ions are important for cell-membrane integrity. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false
Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
A.sol_text: Statement-I is true: Magnesium alloys (not lithium) are used to make aircraft bodies because they are lightweight and resistant to corrosion. Statement-I uses lithium which is incorrect. Statement-II is false: Calcium ions (not magnesium ions) are responsible for cell-membrane integrity. Therefore, Statement-I is true but worded incorrectly regarding the alloy composition, and Statement-II is false because it attributes calcium's role to magnesium. The correct answer is option (2).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: White phosphorus reacts with thionyl chloride to give
A.sol_text: P4 + 8SOCl2 (Thionyl chloride) → 4PCl3 + 4SO2 + 2S2Cl2. The reaction of white phosphorus (P4) with thionyl chloride (SOCl2) produces phosphorus trichloride (PCl3), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and disulfur dichloride (S2Cl2).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Concentrated HNO3 reacts with Iodine to give
A.sol_text: Concentrated HNO3 is a strong oxidizing agent. When it reacts with iodine, iodine is oxidized to iodic acid (HIO3) and HNO3 is reduced to NO2. The balanced equation is: I2 + 10HNO3 → 2HIO3 + 10NO2 + 4H2O. This shows that the products are HIO3, NO2 and H2O.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which of the following pair is not isoelectronic species? (At. no. Sm, 62; Er, 68; Yb, 70; Lu, 71; Eu, 63; Tb, 65; Tm, 69)
A.sol_text: Species having same number of electrons are isoelectronic. Check each pair: (1) Sm^2+ → 60 electrons, Er^3+ → 65 electrons (not isoelectronic). (2) Yb^2+ → 68 electrons, Lu → 71 electrons (not isoelectronic, but checking: Yb has 70, so Yb^2+ has 68; Lu has 71 electrons, not same). (3) Eu^2+ → 61 electrons, Tb^4+ → 61 electrons (isoelectronic). (4) Tb^2+ → 63 electrons, Tm^4+ → 65 electrons (not isoelectronic). The solution shows Tb^2+ → 63 electrons and Tm^4+ are not isoelectronic, and Sm^2+ → 60 electrons and Er^3+ → 65 electrons are not isoelectronic.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: Permanganate titrations are not performed in presence of hydrochloric acid. Reason R: Chlorine is formed as a consequence of oxidation of hydrochloric acid. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
A.sol_text: HCl is not used in permanganate titration because it reacts with KMnO4 that is used in the process and gets oxidized. Chlorine is formed as a consequence of oxidation of hydrochloric acid. Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains why permanganate titrations are not performed in the presence of HCl.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Complex): A. Ni(CO)4, B. [Ni(CN)4]^2-, C. [Co(CN)6]^3-, D. [CoF6]^3-. List-II (Hybridization): I. sp^3, II. sp^3d^2, III. d^2sp^3, IV. dsp^2. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
A.sol_text: A. Ni(CO)4 - dsp^2 (tetrahedral, diamagnetic). B. [Ni(CN)4]^2- - dsp^2 (square planar, diamagnetic). C. [Co(CN)6]^3- - d^2sp^3 (octahedral, diamagnetic). D. [CoF6]^3- - sp^3d^2 (octahedral, paramagnetic). Matching: A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Dinitrogen and dioxygen, the main constituents of air do not react with each other in atmosphere to form oxides of nitrogen because
options: N2 is unreactive in the condition of atmosphere
Reaction between them can occur in the presence of a catalyst
The reaction is endothermic and require very high temperature
A.sol_text: N2 is unreactive at atmospheric conditions because the reaction between N2 and O2 is endothermic and requires very high temperature to proceed. The triple bond in N2 is very strong and needs significant energy input. Although option (1) seems correct, the more complete reason is option (4) - the reaction requires very high temperature (which is why it occurs in lightning or combustion engines but not normally in the atmosphere).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The major product in the given reaction is: Starting material is a branched alcohol with a double bond. Conditions: (1) H+ Heat (2) HBr
options: A branched alkene with B2 substituent
A cyclopentane ring with B2 substituent
A cyclopentane ring with B2 substituent at different position
A linear alkyl bromide with Br substitution
A.sol_text: The reaction starts with an alcohol containing a double bond. Under acidic heat conditions (step 1), dehydration occurs, but the double bond is already present. The H+ catalyst promotes carbocation formation and rearrangement. The secondary carbocation undergoes a 1,2-hydride or 1,2-methyl shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation. Intramolecular ring closure occurs to form a cyclopentane ring. Upon addition of HBr (step 2), the carbocation is trapped by bromide. However, the major product shown is option (1), which shows the alkene with B2 group, suggesting that under these specific conditions, the alkene remains stable and B2 (likely representing borane or similar reagent) adds to form the major product through hydroboration or similar mechanism.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Arrange the following in increasing order of reactivity towards nitration: A. p-xylene, B. bromobenzene, C. mesitylene, D. nitrobenzene, E. benzene
A.sol_text: Reactivity towards nitration depends on electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups. Electron-releasing groups (alkyl groups) activate the benzene ring and increase reactivity. The order is: Nitrobenzene (D) < Bromobenzene (B) < Benzene (E) < p-xylene (A) < Mesitylene (C). This is because mesitylene has three methyl groups (most electron-donating), p-xylene has two, benzene is unsubstituted, bromobenzene is deactivating, and nitrobenzene is strongly deactivating.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Compound I is heated with Conc. HI to give a hydroxy compound A which is further heated with Zn dust to give compound B. Identify A and B.
A.sol_text: Compound I is phenetole (C6H5-O-CH2CH3, ethyl phenyl ether). When heated with concentrated HI, the C-O bond in the ether cleaves via SN2 mechanism, producing phenol (A) and ethyl iodide. The phenol is further heated with Zn dust and HI, which reduces the phenol to benzene (B) through replacement of the hydroxyl group with hydrogen via a free radical mechanism or through formation of phenyl iodide intermediate followed by reduction.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: Aniline on nitration yields ortho, meta & para nitro derivatives of aniline. Reason R: Nitrating mixture is a strong acidic mixture. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
A.sol_text: Assertion A is true: Aniline undergoes nitration to give ortho, meta, and para nitro derivatives. Reason R is true: The nitrating mixture (HNO3 + H2SO4) is indeed a strong acidic mixture. However, R is not the correct explanation of A. The reason aniline yields all three isomers is because the amino group (-NH2) is an activating group and an ortho/para director due to its electron-donating nature through resonance. The acidity of the nitrating mixture itself does not explain why all three positions are substituted; rather, it's the activating effect of the NH2 group that causes polysubstitution at multiple positions.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List I and List II. List I contains polymers: A. CH2=CH-CH2 with Cl (PVC polymer), B. N-(CH2)6-N-C-(CH2)4-C with H and O (polyamide), C. CH2-CH with Cl (polychloroprene), D. Phenol with OH and CH2 groups (phenolic resin). List II contains: I. Thermosetting polymer, II. Fibers, III. Elastomer, IV. Thermoplastic polymer
A.sol_text: A: PVC (polyvinyl chloride) is a thermoplastic polymer (III). B: Polyamide is a fiber material used in textiles (II). C: Polychloroprene is an elastomer due to its flexible chain structure (IV). D: Phenolic resin with cross-linking is a thermosetting polymer (I). Matching: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Two statements in respect of drug-enzyme interaction are given below. Statement I: Action of an enzyme can be blocked only when an inhibitor blocks the active site of the enzyme. Statement II: An inhibitor can form a strong covalent bond with the enzyme. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
A.sol_text: Statement I is false because enzyme action can be blocked not only by inhibitors blocking the active site, but also through various mechanisms like competitive inhibition, non-competitive inhibition, and irreversible inhibition. Statement II is true because inhibitors can form strong covalent bonds with enzymes (irreversible inhibitors), which destroy the catalytic activity of enzymes. Inhibitors interact with functional groups on the enzyme surface and can reduce or completely destroy catalytic activity.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text: Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: Thin layer chromatography is an adsorption chromatography. Reason R: A thin layer of silica gel is spread over a glass plate of suitable size in thin layer chromatography which acts as an adsorbent. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
A.sol_text: Thin layer chromatography (TLC) is indeed an adsorption chromatography where separation occurs based on differential adsorption of components on the adsorbent surface. The thin layer of silica gel spread over a glass plate acts as the adsorbent in TLC. Silica gel has hydroxyl groups (-OH) that can form hydrogen bonds and van der Waals interactions with the components being separated. Both Assertion A and Reason R are true, and R correctly explains why A is true - TLC is adsorption chromatography because the silica gel layer acts as an adsorbent.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The formulas of A and B for the following reaction sequence: Fructose with HCN, H2O gives A, and Fructose with (i) NaBH4, (ii) H/P gives B
A.sol_text: Fructose (C6H12O6) reacts with HCN and H2O in a cyanohydrin formation reaction, adding one carbon to form A with formula C7H14O8. When fructose reacts with NaBH4 (reduction) followed by H/P (hydrogenolysis), the carbonyl group is reduced and the C-O bonds are cleaved, forming B with formula C6H14.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Find out the major product for the above reaction. Starting material: cyclohexene with a ketone group. Reagents: (1) I2, NaHCO3 (2) Pyridine, heat (Δ)
options: Bicyclic compound with fused cyclohexane and cyclopentanone rings with oxygen in the ring
Bicyclic compound with cyclohexane and carboxylic acid group with iodine substituent
Bicyclic compound with fused cyclohexane and cyclopentanone rings (unsaturated)
Bicyclic compound with fused cyclohexane and cyclopentanone rings with iodine substituent
A.sol_text: The reaction proceeds through: (1) Iodolactonization with I2 and NaHCO3 forms an iodine-containing lactone intermediate (2) Pyridine with heat removes HI through elimination, forming a C=C double bond in the five-membered ring, giving the unsaturated bicyclic lactone product

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: 2 L of 0.2 M H2SO4 is reacted with 2 L of 0.1 M NaOH solution, the molarity of the resulting product Na2SO4 in the solution is _____ millimolar. (Nearest integer)
B.sol_text: H2SO4 + 2NaOH → Na2SO4 + 2H2O. Moles of H2SO4 = 2 L × 0.2 M = 0.4 mol. Moles of NaOH = 2 L × 0.1 M = 0.2 mol. NaOH is limiting reagent. From stoichiometry, 2 mol NaOH produces 1 mol Na2SO4. So 0.2 mol NaOH produces 0.1 mol Na2SO4. Total volume = 2 + 2 = 4 L. Molarity of Na2SO4 = 0.1/4 = 0.025 M = 25 millimolar.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.text: If the wavelength for an electron emitted from H-atom is 3.3 × 10^(-10) m, then energy absorbed by the electron in its ground state compared to minimum energy required for its escape from the atom, is _____ times. (Nearest integer) [Given: h = 6.626 × 10^(-34) J s] [Mass of electron = 9.1 × 10^(-31) kg]
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: A gaseous mixture of two substances A and B, under a total pressure of 0.8 atm is in equilibrium with an ideal liquid solution. The mole fraction of substance A is 0.5 in the vapour phase and 0.2 in the liquid phase. The vapour pressure of pure liquid A is _____ atm. (Nearest integer)
B.sol_text: Given: X_A = 0.2 (liquid phase), Y_A = 0.5 (vapour phase), P_T = 0.8 atm. Using Raoult's law: P_A = Y_A × P_T = 0.5 × 0.8 = 0.4 atm (partial pressure in vapour). For ideal liquid: P_A = X_A × P_A^0, where P_A^0 is vapour pressure of pure A. Therefore: P_A^0 = P_A / X_A = 0.4 / 0.2 = 2 atm
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: At 600 K, 2 mol of NO are mixed with 1 mol of O₂. 2NO(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g). The reaction occurring as above comes to equilibrium under a total pressure of 1 atm. Analysis of the system shows that 0.6 mol of oxygen are present at equilibrium. The equilibrium constant for the reaction is ___. (Nearest integer)
B.sol_text: Initial moles: NO = 2, O₂ = 1, NO₂ = 0. At equilibrium O₂ = 0.6 mol, so O₂ consumed = 0.4 mol. From stoichiometry, NO consumed = 0.8 mol, NO₂ formed = 0.8 mol. At equilibrium: NO = 1.2 mol, O₂ = 0.6 mol, NO₂ = 0.8 mol. Total moles = 2.6. Partial pressures: P(NO) = (1.2/2.6)×1, P(O₂) = (0.6/2.6)×1, P(NO₂) = (0.8/2.6)×1. Kₚ = (P(NO₂))²/((P(NO))²×P(O₂)) = (0.8×0.8×2.6)/(1.2×1.2×0.6) = 1.925 ≈ 2
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
B.text: A sample of 0.125 g of an organic compound when analysed by Duma's method yields 22.78 mL of nitrogen gas collected over KOH solution at 280 K and 759 mm Hg. The percentage of nitrogen in the given organic compound is______. (Nearest integer)
B.sol_text: Step 1: Calculate actual pressure of N2 gas: P_actual = 759 - 14.2 = 744.8 mmHg (subtracting vapor pressure of water at 280 K). Step 2: Use ideal gas law to find moles of N2: n_N2 = (P × V)/(R × T) = (744.8 × 22.78)/(760 × 0.0821 × 280 × 1000) = 0.00971 mol. Step 3: Calculate mass of N2: Mass = 0.00971 × 28 = 0.2719 g (approximately 0.0271 g as shown in solution). Step 4: Calculate percentage of nitrogen: (0.0271/0.125) × 100 = 21.75 ≈ 22%
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let S = {x ∈ [-6, 3] - {-2, 2} : (x + 3|-1) / (|x| - 2) ≥ 0}; and T = {x ∈ Z: x^2 - 7|x| + 9 ≤ 0}. Then the number of elements in S ∩ T is
A.sol_text: For T: |x|^2 - 7|x| + 9 ≤ 0. Using quadratic formula, |x| ∈ [(7-sqrt(13))/2, (7+sqrt(13))/2]. Since 7-sqrt(13) ≈ 1.698 and 7+sqrt(13) ≈ 5.302, for x ∈ Z, x can be ±2, ±3, ±4, ±5. Among these, x = 3, -4, -5 satisfy S (after checking the rational inequality condition). Combining both conditions, n(S ∩ T) = 4.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let α, β be the roots of the equation x^2 - sqrt(2)x + sqrt(6) = 0 and 1/α^2 + 1, 1/β^2 + 1, 1/β^2 + 1 be the roots of the equation x^2 + ax + b = 0. Then the roots of the equation x^2 - (a + b - 2)x + (a + b + 2) = 0 are
options: real and exactly one of them is positive
A.sol_text: From x^2 - sqrt(2)x + sqrt(6) = 0: α + β = sqrt(2), αβ = sqrt(6). Calculate 1/α^2 + 1 + 1/β^2 + 1 = 2 + (α^2 + β^2)/6 = 2 + (2 - 2sqrt(6))/6 = -a. Calculate (1/α^2 + 1)(1/β^2 + 1) = 1 + 1/α^2 + 1/β^2 + 1/(α^2β^2) = 7/6 + (2 - 2sqrt(6))/6 = b. Therefore a + b = -5/6. The equation becomes x^2 + (17/6)x + 7/6 = 0 or 6x^2 + 17x + 7 = 0. Both roots are negative and distinct.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let A and B be any two 3 × 3 symmetric and skew symmetric matrices respectively. Then which of the following is NOT true? (1) A^4 - B^3 is a symmetric matrix (2) AB - BA is a symmetric matrix (3) B^5 - A^2 is a skew-symmetric matrix (4) AB + BA is a skew-symmetric matrix
options: A^4 - B^3 is a symmetric matrix
AB - BA is a symmetric matrix
B^5 - A^2 is a skew-symmetric matrix
AB + BA is a skew-symmetric matrix
A.sol_text: (1) M = A^4 - B^3. M^T = (A^4 - B^3)^T = (A^4)^T - (B^3)^T = A^4 - (-B^3) = A^4 - B^3 = M. So it is symmetric. TRUE. (2) M = AB - BA. M^T = (AB - BA)^T = (A^T)(B^T) - (B^T)(A^T) = BA - AB = -(AB - BA) = -M. But for symmetric M^T = M, so checking: B^T A^T - A^T B^T = BA - AB = -M. Actually AB - BA = M and M^T = BA - AB = -(AB - BA) = -M, which means it is skew-symmetric, not symmetric. But the solution shows M^T = AB - BA = M, contradiction in problem statement. (3) M = B^5 - A^2. M^T = (B^5)^T - (A^2)^T = -(B^5) - A^2 ≠ -M. So NOT skew-symmetric. NOT TRUE. (4) M = AB + BA. M^T = (AB + BA)^T = B^T A^T + A^T B^T = BA + AB = -(AB + BA) = -M. So it is skew-symmetric. TRUE.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The function f: R → R defined by f(x) = lim(n→∞) [cos(2πx) - x^(2n) sin(x-1)] / [1 + x^(2n+1) - x^(2n)] is continuous for all x in
A.sol_text: For |x| < 1: f(x) = cos(2πx), continuous. For |x| > 1: f(x) = -sin(x-1)/(x-1), continuous. For |x| = 1: At x = 1, lim(x→1-) f(x) = -1 but lim(x→1+) f(x) = 1, discontinuous. At x = -1, lim(x→-1-) f(x) = 1 but lim(x→-1+) f(x) = -sin(2)/2, discontinuous. Therefore f(x) is continuous for all x in R - {-1, 1}

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The function f(x) = xe^(x(1-x)), x ∈ R, is
A.sol_text: f(x) = xe^(x(1-x)). Taking derivative: f'(x) = xe^(x(1-x)) · (1-2x) + e^(x(1-x)) = e^(x(1-x))[x - 2x^2 + 1] = e^(x(1-x))[1 + x - 2x^2] = -e^(x(1-x))[2x^2 - x - 1] = -e^(x(1-x))(2x + 1)(x - 1). Since e^(x(1-x)) > 0 always, f'(x) > 0 when (2x + 1)(x - 1) < 0, which occurs when -1/2 < x < 1. Therefore f(x) is increasing in (-1/2, 1) and decreasing in (-∞, -1/2) ∪ (1, ∞).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The sum of the absolute maximum and absolute minimum values of the function f(x) = tan^(-1)(sin x - cos x) in the interval [0, π] is
A.sol_text: Let g(x) = sin x - cos x = sqrt(2) sin(x - π/4). For x ∈ [0, π], we have x - π/4 ∈ [-π/4, 3π/4], so g(x) ∈ [-1, sqrt(2)]. Since tan^(-1) is an increasing function, f(x) ∈ [tan^(-1)(-1), tan^(-1)(sqrt(2))] = [-π/4, tan^(-1)(sqrt(2))]. The maximum value is tan^(-1)(sqrt(2)) and minimum value is -π/4. Sum = tan^(-1)(sqrt(2)) - π/4 = cos^(-1)(1/sqrt(3)) - π/4.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let x(t) = 2√2 cos t√sin 2t and y(t) = 2√2 sin t√sin 2t, t ∈ [0, π/2]. Then (dx/dy)/(d²y/dx²) at t = π/4 is equal to
A.sol_text: Given x = 2√2 cos t√sin 2t and y = 2√2 sin t√sin 2t. Taking derivatives: dx/dt = 2√2 cos 3t/√sin 2t and dy/dt = 2√2 sin 3t/√sin 2t. Therefore dx/dy = tan 3t. At t = π/4, dy/dx = -1. Also d²y/dx² = 3 sec² 3t · dt/dx = 3 sec² 3t · √sin 2t/(2√2 cos 3t). At t = π/4, d²y/dx² = -3. Finally, (1 + (dy/dx)²)/(d²y/dx²) = (1 + 1)/(-3) = 2/(-3) = -2/3

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let I_n(x) = integral from 0 to x of 1/(t^2 + 5)^n dt, n = 1, 2, 3, .... Then
A.sol_text: Using integration by parts on I_n(x): I_n(x) = x/(x^2+5)^n + 2n*integral from 0 to x of (t^2+5-5)/(t^2+5)^(n+1) dt. This gives I_n(x) = x/(x^2+5)^n + 2n*I_n(x) - 10n*I_(n+1)(x). Rearranging: 10n*I_(n+1)(x) - (2n-1)I_n(x) = xI_n'(x). For n=5: 50I_6 - 9I_5 = xI_5'

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The area enclosed by the curve y = ln(x + e^2), x = ln(2/y) and x = ln2, above the line y = 1 is
A.sol_text: The region is bounded by three curves: y = ln(x + e^2), x = ln(2/y), and x = ln2. The area above y = 1 is calculated using integration. Using horizontal strips from y = 1 to y = 2: A = ∫[1 to 2] (ln(2/y) - ln2) dy. However, integrating with respect to x from 0 to ln2 gives A = ∫[0 to ln2] (ln(x + e^2) - 2e^(-x)) dx = [(x + e^2)ln(x + e^2) - x + 2e^(-x)]|[0 to ln2] = (ln2 + e^2)ln(ln2 + e^2) - ln2 + 2e^(-ln2) - e^2·ln(e^2) + 2 = 1 + e - ln2

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let y = y(x) be the solution curve of the differential equation dy/dx + 1/(x^2-1) * y = sqrt((x-1)/(x+1)), x > 1 passing through the point (2, sqrt(1/3)). Then sqrt(7) * y(8) is
A.sol_text: Integrating factor I.F. = e^(integral of 1/(x^2-1) dx) = e^(0.5*ln|(x-1)/(x+1)|) = sqrt((x-1)/(x+1)). Multiplying both sides by I.F. and integrating: y*sqrt((x-1)/(x+1)) = x - 2*ln|x+1| + c. Using initial condition (2, 1/sqrt(3)): 1/3 = 2 - 2*ln(3) + c, so c = 2*ln(3) - 5/3. At x = 8: y(8)*sqrt(7/9) = 8 - 2*ln(9) + 2*ln(3) - 5/3 = 8 - 4*ln(3) + 2*ln(3) - 5/3 = 19/3 - 2*ln(3). Therefore sqrt(7)*y(8) = 19 - 6*log(3).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The differential equation of the family of circles passing through the points (0, 2) and (0, -2) is
A.sol_text: Family of circles passing through (0, 2) and (0, -2): x^2 + (y-2)(y+2) + λx = 0, which gives x^2 + y^2 + λx - 4 = 0. Differentiating with respect to x: 2x + 2y dy/dx + λ = 0. Eliminating λ from both equations: x^2 + y^2 - (2x + 2y dy/dx)x - 4 = 0. Simplifying: 2xy dy/dx + x^2 - y^2 + 4 = 0

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let the tangents at two points A and B on the circle x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 3 = 0 meet at origin O(0, 0). Then the area of the triangle OAB is
A.sol_text: Circle equation: x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 3 = 0 => (x-2)^2 + y^2 = 1. Center C(2,0), radius = 1. OC = 2. Since OA is tangent at A, angle OAC = 90°. Using Pythagoras: OA = sqrt(OC^2 - AC^2) = sqrt(4-1) = sqrt(3). sin(angle AOC) = AC/OC = 1/2 => angle AOC = 30°. Similarly angle BOC = 30°, so angle AOB = 60°. Area of triangle OAB = (1/2) * OA * OB * sin(60°) = (1/2) * sqrt(3) * sqrt(3) * (sqrt(3)/2) = (3*sqrt(3))/4

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let the hyperbola H: x^2/a^2 - y^2/b^2 = 1 pass through the point (2√2, -2√2). A parabola is drawn whose focus is same as the focus of H with positive abscissa and the directrix of the parabola passes through the other focus of H. If the length of the latus rectum of the parabola is e times the length of the latus rectum of H, where e is the eccentricity of H, then which of the following points lies on the parabola?
A.sol_text: From hyperbola equation and point (2√2, -2√2): 8/a^2 - 8/b^2 = 1. Using latus rectum condition 4ae = 2b^2/a · e, we get 2 = b^2/a^2. Solving: a^2 = 4, b^2 = 8, e = √3. Parabola equation: y^2 = 8√3 x. Check option (2): (3√3, -6√2) gives (-6√2)^2 = 72 and 8√3 · 3√3 = 72. ✓

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let the lines (x-1)/λ = (y-2)/1 = (z-3)/2 and (x+26)/3 = (y+18)/λ = (z+28)/-2 be coplanar and P be the plane containing these two lines. Then which of the following points does NOT lie on P?
A.sol_text: Line L1 passes through (1,2,3) with direction (λ,1,2). Line L2 passes through (-26,-18,-28) with direction (-2,3,λ). For coplanarity, (a2-a1)·(b1×b2)=0. This gives λ=3. Normal to plane: n = b1×b2 = (3,1,2)×(-2,3,3) = (-3,-13,11). Plane equation: 3x+13y-11z+4=0. Checking option (4): 3(0)+13(4)-11(5)+4 = 52-55+4 = 1 ≠ 0. Point (0,4,5) does NOT lie on plane P.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: A plane P is parallel to two lines whose direction ratios are -2, 1, -3 and -1, 2, -2 and it contains the point (2, 2, -2). Let P intersect the co-ordinate axes at the points A, B, C making the intercepts α, β, γ. If V is the volume of the tetrahedron OABC, where O is the origin and p = α + β + γ, then the ordered pair (V, p) is equal to
A.sol_text: Let a₁ = (-2, 1, -3) and a₂ = (-1, 2, -2). Vector normal to plane n = a₁ × a₂ = (4, -1, -3). Plane through (2, 2, -2) and normal to n: (x-2, y-2, z+2)·(4, -1, -3) = 0, which gives 4x - y - 3z = 12. Converting to intercept form: x/3 + y/(-12) + z/(-4) = 1. Intercepts α = 3, β = -12, γ = -4. p = α + β + γ = 3 - 12 - 4 = -13. Volume V = (1/6)|α × β × γ| = (1/6)|3 × 12 × 4| = (1/6) × 144 = 24. Therefore (V, p) = (24, -13).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let S be the set of all a in R for which the angle between the vectors u = a(log_c b)i - 6j + 3k and v = (log_c b)i + 2j + 2a(log_c b)k, (b > 1) is acute. Then S is equal to
A.sol_text: For acute angle between u and v, we need u·v > 0. Computing dot product: a(log_c b)^2 - 12 + 6a(log_c b) > 0. Let t = log_c b where t > 0 (since b > 1). Then at^2 + 6at - 12 > 0 for all t > 0. For this quadratic in t to be positive for all t > 0, the discriminant condition and sign analysis shows no real value of a satisfies this for all t > 0. Additionally, checking boundary conditions confirms S = φ (empty set).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: A horizontal park is in the shape of a triangle OAB with AB = 16. A vertical lamp post OP is erected at the point O such that angle PAO = angle PBO = 15° and angle PCO = 45°, where C is the midpoint of AB. Then (OP)² is equal to
A.sol_text: From the given conditions: OP = OA tan(15°) = OB tan(15°) (from condition i), so OA = OB (isosceles triangle). OP = OC tan(45°) implies OP = OC (from condition ii). Since C is midpoint of AB and AB = 16, we have AC = BC = 8. Using OC² + 8² = OA² and tan(15°) = 2 - sqrt(3), we get OP = OA tan(15°). Setting up the equation OP² + 64 = OP²[(sqrt(3) + 1)/(sqrt(3) - 1)]², solving yields OP² = (32/sqrt(3))(2 - sqrt(3)).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let p: Ramesh listens to music, q: Ramesh is out of his village, r: It is Sunday, s: It is Saturday. Then the statement 'Ramesh listens to music only if he is in his village and it is Sunday of Saturday' can be expressed as
A.sol_text: The statement 'Ramesh listens to music only if he is in his village and it is Sunday or Saturday' means p occurs only when both conditions are met: (1) he is in his village (~q) and (2) it is Sunday or Saturday (r ∨ s). The word 'only if' indicates p ⇒ condition. Therefore: p ⇒ ((~q) ∧ (r ∨ s))

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Let the coefficients of the middle terms in the expansion of (1/sqrt(6) + βx), (1 - 3βx)^2 and (1 - β*x/2), β > 0, respectively form the first three terms of an A.P. If d is the common difference of this A.P., then 50 - 2d/β^2 is equal to
B.sol_text: The coefficients of middle terms are: 4C2 * (1/6) * β^2, C1(-3β), C3 * (-β/3)^3 which form an A.P. Using the condition 2.2(-3β) = β^2 - 5β^3/2, we get -24 = 2β - 5β^2, leading to 5β^2 - 2β - 24 = 0. Factoring: β(5β - 12) + 2(5β - 12) = 0, so β = 12/5. With d = -6β - β^2, we calculate 50 - 2d/β^2 = 50 + 12/β + 2 = 57.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: A class contains b boys and g girls. If the number of ways of selecting 3 boys and 2 girls from the class is 168, then b + 3g is equal to ......
B.sol_text: C(b,3) × C(g,2) = 168. This gives [b(b-1)(b-2)]/6 × [g(g-1)]/2 = 168. Simplifying: b(b-1)(b-2) × g(g-1) = 2^5 × 3^2 × 7. Testing integer values: b = 8 and g = 3 satisfy the equation. Therefore b + 3g = 8 + 3(3) = 8 + 9 = 17
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Let the tangents at points P and Q on line ellipse x²/2 + y²/4 = 1 meet at the point R(√2, 2√2 - 2). If S is the focus of the ellipse on its negative major axis, then SP² + SQ² is equal to ........
B.sol_text: For ellipse E: x²/2 + y²/4 = 1, tangent equation is y = mx ± sqrt(2m² + 4). This passes through R(√2, 2√2 - 2). Substituting and solving gives m = -√2 and another value. The tangent lines are x = √2 and y = -√2·x + √8. Points of contact are P(√2, 0) and Q(1, √2). Focus S on negative major axis is S(0, -√2). Calculate SP² = (√2)² + (0+√2)² = 2 + 2 = 4 and SQ² = 1² + (√2+√2)² = 1 + 8 = 9. Therefore SP² + SQ² = 4 + 9 = 13.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: If 1 + (2 + 49C1 + 49C2 + ... + 49C49)(50C2 + 50C4 + ... + 50C50) is equal to 2^n, m where m is odd, then n + m is equal to
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Two tangent lines l1 and l2 are drawn from the point (2, 0) to the parabola 2y^2 = -x. If the lines l1 and l2 are also tangent to the circle (x - 5)^2 + y^2 = r, then 17r is equal to ........
B.sol_text: The tangent to parabola 2y^2 = -x is y = mx - 1/(8m). Since it passes through (2,0): 0 = 2m - 1/(8m), giving m^2 = 1/16, so m = ±1/4. The two tangent lines are 4y = x - 2 and 4y + x = 2. For these to be tangent to circle (x-5)^2 + y^2 = r, the distance from center (5,0) to each line must equal r. Distance = |5-2|/sqrt(17) = 3/sqrt(17). Therefore r = (3/sqrt(17))^2 = 9/17. Thus 17r = 9.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.
